ITodoAppGuestUser.IJoinRequest.description:
Request payload for registering a new guest user concept in the todoApp backend.

This DTO is used by the /auth/guestUser/join endpoint to create a minimal guest record in the todo_app_guestusers table and immediately establish an authorized guestUser context. It carries only client-provided metadata that can be safely persisted alongside server-controlled fields such as id, created_at, and updated_at.

The primary business purpose of this type is to optionally attach a correlation identifier to the conceptual guest actor so that external analytics or tracking systems can map requests to a stable, server-managed UUID. It intentionally does not include any authentication credentials, personal information, or system-managed fields; those are handled internally by the service when inserting the guest record and issuing tokens.

external_ref.description:
Optional external reference or correlation identifier for this guest concept.

This value corresponds to the external_ref column in the todo_app_guestusers table and allows client systems or analytics pipelines to associate a created guestUser with their own tracking identifiers. It should be treated as opaque by the backend and is typically a bounded-length string such as an anonymous tracking ID, browser fingerprint key, or A/B test bucket key.

When omitted or null, the guest will still be created with a generated UUID and timestamps, but there will be no external reference stored in the database. Validation logic should ensure that when provided, the value respects any maximum length and character set expectations enforced at the application or database level.

ITodoAppGuestUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized guestUser representation returned by authentication endpoints for the todoApp service.

This DTO is produced by guest authentication flows such as /auth/guestUser/join and /auth/guestUser/refresh. It encapsulates the guest identity, represented by a stable UUID stored in the todo_app_guestusers table, together with freshly issued access and refresh tokens that the client must use for subsequent API calls.

The structure exposes both the persisted guest concept fields (`id`, `external_ref`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) and a standardized authorization token container via the IAuthorizationToken schema. Implementations must ensure that token-related fields remain consistent so that clients can reliably authenticate and reason about token lifetimes without needing to know internal storage details.

In typical usage, clients read the `id` to correlate guest activity and use either the top-level token string fields or the nested `token` object when attaching credentials to requests. The embedded `IAuthorizationToken` object is considered the canonical representation of token data, while the top-level token properties exist as convenience mirrors for simpler integrations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest concept in the todoApp system.

This UUID corresponds to the primary key of the underlying guest concept record stored in the todo_app_guestusers table. It is stable for the lifetime of the guest concept and may be embedded into access and refresh tokens or used to correlate guest activity across analytics and logging subsystems.

external_ref.description:
Optional external correlation reference for this guest concept.

This field maps to the nullable `external_ref` column in the `todo_app_guestusers` table. It may contain an external tracking identifier, analytics correlation key, or another non-PII token used to link guest interactions across systems.

When no persistent guest identity is required, this field is stored as null and omitted from correlation workflows. Its presence or absence does not affect token issuance, but downstream systems can use it to join guest activity with separate tracking data sources.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the guest user concept record.

This field maps to the non-null `created_at` column in the `todo_app_guestusers` schema and records when the guest concept entry was first created in the system.

It is used for audit trails, retention policy enforcement, and chronological reporting of guest activity initialization, and is always populated by the server when the guest concept is inserted.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the guest user concept record.

This field maps to the non-null `updated_at` column in the `todo_app_guestusers` table and is refreshed whenever metadata for the guest concept is modified or when business rules choose to mark a new interaction time.

It enables tracking of the most recent time the guest-related data was touched for maintenance, analytics corrections, or other operational purposes, and can be used for deciding when to clean up old guest concepts.

accessToken.description:
Short-lived access token for authenticating subsequent guestUser API requests.

This value is a convenient top-level mirror of `token.access` from the embedded IAuthorizationToken structure. Implementations must ensure that `accessToken` and `token.access` are always kept in sync so that clients can safely use either form.

Clients typically send this token in the HTTP Authorization header as `Bearer {accessToken}` when calling protected endpoints until it expires, while relying on the `token.expired_at` field to understand its lifetime.

refreshToken.description:
Longer-lived refresh token used to obtain new access and refresh tokens.

This property is a convenience mirror of `token.refresh` from the IAuthorizationToken payload. The service must keep `refreshToken` and `token.refresh` synchronized so that they always represent the same underlying refresh token value.

Clients pass this value to the /auth/guestUser/refresh endpoint (via ITodoAppGuestUser.IRefreshRequest) to obtain a new ITodoAppGuestUser.IAuthorized response when the current access token is close to or past its expiration, following the refresh and rotation rules defined by the authentication subsystem.

ITodoAppGuestUser.IRefreshRequest.description:
Request body schema for refreshing guestUser authorization tokens in the todoApp service.

This structure encapsulates the refresh token that was previously issued to a guestUser, along with optional client and token-family metadata used by the authorization subsystem to validate and rotate tokens. It is consumed by the /auth/guestUser/refresh endpoint, which validates the provided refresh token against the current guest state represented by the todo_app_guestusers table and associated infrastructure.

The DTO itself does not expose any internal guest identifiers or database fields. Instead, it focuses solely on token and client context required to securely derive the guest identity and issue a renewed ITodoAppGuestUser.IAuthorized payload.

refreshToken.description:
Refresh token string previously issued to the guestUser.

This opaque, signed token is validated by the authorization service to confirm the guest identity, token expiry, revocation status, and token-family constraints. Clients must send exactly the value they received from the prior ITodoAppGuestUser.IAuthorized response without modification.

clientId.description:
Optional logical client identifier associated with the token family.

Used by the authorization subsystem to distinguish tokens issued to different client applications or devices, allowing per-client revocation and rotation policies. When provided, it must exactly match the client identifier that was associated with the original tokens.

tokenFamily.description:
Optional token family identifier for refresh token rotation logic.

Represents a stable identifier that groups a sequence of rotated refresh tokens for the same guest identity within a particular client context. Implementations may use this to detect reuse of old tokens and to invalidate whole families when abuse is detected.

ITodoAppMemberUserJoin.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for registering a new memberUser account in the todoApp service.

This DTO is consumed by the /auth/memberUser/join endpoint. It collects the minimal information required to create a new authenticated member in the todo_app_memberusers table, namely the email address, a plaintext password, and an optional displayName to show in user interfaces.

The backend transforms the provided password into a secure password_hash field in the todo_app_memberusers model and sets initial lifecycle fields such as status, created_at, and updated_at. The DTO does not expose internal database fields like password_hash or status and does not accept system-managed identifiers or timestamps.

In addition, because this is a self-signup operation that establishes an authenticated context and typically creates an initial member session, the DTO also carries session metadata fields (ip, href, referrer). These values are used to populate the corresponding session records for auditability and security analysis without exposing any authentication-context identifiers such as user IDs or session IDs.

email.description:
Email address for the new member user account.

This value is used both as the primary login identifier and as a communication channel for account-related notifications. It must be unique across all records in the todo_app_memberusers table, where it is enforced by a unique index, and must conform to standard email formatting rules.

password.description:
Plaintext password for the new member user account.

The backend hashes this value into the password_hash column of the todo_app_memberusers table using a strong one-way hashing algorithm. The raw password is never stored. Implementations may apply additional validation rules such as minimum length or complexity requirements.

displayName.description:
Optional human-friendly name or nickname for the member user.

When provided, it maps to the display_name column in todo_app_memberusers and is used in user-facing contexts instead of the raw email. When omitted, the account may still be created with a null display_name, and user interfaces may fall back to showing the email address.

ip.description:
Optional client IP address observed when the member user performs self-registration.

This value represents the network-level source address of the join request and is primarily used for security auditing, anomaly detection, and session analytics. When supplied, it can be stored alongside the initial member session record; when omitted, the server implementation may instead derive the IP from the transport layer.

The field is intentionally optional and nullable so that clients may either provide an explicit value (for example, in SSR or proxy-aware contexts) or leave it null and rely on the backend to infer the effective IP address.

href.description:
Current page URL at the time the memberUser join request is initiated.

This value captures the full connection URL from which the registration action was triggered (for example, the sign-up page URL in a web client). It is used when creating the initial member session to record the entry point of the interaction for security auditing, behavioral analytics, and troubleshooting.

Because the backend cannot reliably infer the precise client-facing URL (especially in SPA, proxy, or CDN scenarios), the client is required to send this value explicitly as part of the self-signup request.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL immediately preceding the memberUser join request.

This value represents the page or location from which the user navigated before reaching the registration screen, mirroring the semantics of the HTTP Referer/Referrer header in a client-controlled and auditable way. It is persisted with the initial session so that operators can reconstruct typical onboarding paths and detect suspicious navigation patterns.

When there is no meaningful referrer (for example, direct navigation or native app flows), clients should send an empty string or a conventional placeholder URL consistent with the overall tracking strategy, rather than omitting the field.

ITodoAppMemberUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized member user representation returned after successful authentication or token refresh in the todoApp service.

This DTO encapsulates the authenticated principal derived from the `todo_app_memberusers` table together with freshly issued access and refresh tokens that the client can use to access member-protected endpoints.

The structure is designed to be consumed by frontend clients as a single source of truth for the current member identity and credentials immediately after join, login, or refresh operations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member user account.

This value corresponds to `todo_app_memberusers.id` and is used as the stable principal key when performing member-protected operations such as managing todos.

email.description:
Email address of the authenticated member user.

Sourced from `todo_app_memberusers.email`, this value is the primary login identifier for the member and may also be presented in account management UIs.

display_name.description:
Optional human-friendly display name or nickname of the member user.

If set, this value is typically sourced from `todo_app_memberusers.display_name`. It may be null when the member has not configured any custom name and the client should fall back to showing the email address instead.

status.description:
Business status of the member account.

Reflects values stored in `todo_app_memberusers.status`, such as `"active"`, `"blocked"`, or `"disabled"`. Clients can use this to adjust UX (for example, warning when an account is nearing a restricted state), while backend authorization enforces the actual access rules.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the member user account was created.

Directly mapped from `todo_app_memberusers.created_at`, this is useful for auditing, account age display, and chronological reporting.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the member user account.

Mapped from `todo_app_memberusers.updated_at`, this changes whenever profile or status information is modified and can be used for cache invalidation or display of "last updated" information.

ITodoAppMemberUserLogin.ICreate.description:
Login payload for authenticating an existing member user in the todoApp service.

Clients submit the member's email and password, along with optional connection metadata, to request an authenticated session. The backend validates these credentials against todo_app_memberusers (using email and password_hash) and typically creates a session entry in todo_app_memberuser_sessions using the supplied connection context.

This DTO never includes any identity fields such as member IDs, because those are derived by the server from the validated credentials, and it never contains pre-hashed passwords. The raw password is provided in plain text and hashed server-side.

email.description:
Email address of the member user attempting to log in.

This value is matched against todo_app_memberusers.email and serves as the primary credential identifier during authentication. It must be a syntactically valid email address and is subject to the uniqueness constraint enforced on the member table.

password.description:
Plain-text password for the member user.

The server hashes this value and compares it to todo_app_memberusers.password_hash; hashed passwords must never be sent by clients. Implementations may enforce additional policies such as minimum length, character variety, or breach checks, but those rules are enforced on the server side, not encoded in this schema.

ip.description:
Optional client IP address associated with this login attempt.

When provided, it may be recorded in todo_app_memberuser_sessions.ip for auditing, security analytics, or anomaly detection. If omitted or null, the server can derive the IP from the underlying HTTP request or reverse proxy headers, depending on deployment configuration.

href.description:
Absolute URL of the page from which the login request is initiated.

This connection context is typically persisted in todo_app_memberuser_sessions.href and can help operators understand from which route or screen the authentication attempt originated. It must be a valid URI string, usually matching the frontend application location.

referrer.description:
Referring URL that led the client to the login page.

This value is often stored in todo_app_memberuser_sessions.referrer and may be an empty page or external site that navigated to the login screen. It is useful for analyzing user flows and potential security concerns such as phishing, but is not required for successful authentication.

ITodoAppMemberUserRefresh.ICreate.description:
Request payload for refreshing authentication tokens for a member user in the todoApp service.

This DTO carries the refresh token issued during a previous authentication flow and optional session correlation metadata so the backend can validate that the token is still associated with an active or acceptable session.

The server validates the refresh token against member identity records stored in the `todo_app_memberusers` table and may optionally cross-check an associated session in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` before issuing a new `ITodoAppMemberUser.IAuthorized` response.

refresh_token.description:
Opaque refresh token previously issued to the member user.

The backend uses this token to locate and verify the corresponding member record in `todo_app_memberusers` and, optionally, a session record in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions`. The exact format is implementation specific (for example, a JWT or random string) and should be treated as a confidential credential by clients.

session_id.description:
Optional identifier of the member user session associated with this refresh attempt.

When provided, this UUID typically corresponds to a row in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions.id`. The server can use it to ensure that the refresh token is being used from the same logical session context and to reject tokens tied to expired or revoked sessions.

ip.description:
Optional client IP address observed when performing the refresh.

Although the canonical IP may be derived from the HTTP request on the server, clients or intermediaries can supply this field to capture the most accurate origin information for auditing and anomaly detection. When present, it is compared against past session metadata as part of security checks.

href.description:
Optional full URL (href) of the page or route where the refresh request is initiated.

This helps correlate refresh operations with specific user interface locations in the client application. It may be used for security analytics or troubleshooting but is not required for token validation.

referrer.description:
Optional referrer URL indicating the previous page or context leading to this refresh call.

This can be used in conjunction with `href` for navigation analysis and security monitoring but is not required for successful token refresh.

ITodoAppAdminUser.IJoin.description:
Request payload for registering a new administrative user in the todoApp service and establishing an initial admin session.

This DTO carries the minimal credential and profile information required to create a row in `todo_app_adminusers`, along with connection metadata used to create an associated session in `todo_app_adminuser_sessions`.

It is used by the `/auth/adminUser/join` endpoint, which persists the admin account, records the session, and returns an `ITodoAppAdminUser.IAuthorized` response with issued tokens.

email.description:
Email address for the new admin user account.

This value is stored in `todo_app_adminusers.email`, which is unique and non-nullable. It serves as the primary login identifier for administrative access and must not collide with an existing admin email.

password.description:
Plaintext password for the new admin account.

The backend hashes this value using a secure one-way algorithm and stores the result in `todo_app_adminusers.password_hash`. The raw password is never persisted and should be transmitted only over secure connections.

display_name.description:
Optional human-readable name for the admin user.

If provided, it is stored in `todo_app_adminusers.display_name` and may be shown in logs, dashboards, or audit trails. When null, administrative UIs typically fall back to the email address.

status.description:
Initial business status of the admin account.

This value populates `todo_app_adminusers.status` on creation and determines whether the admin can authenticate immediately. Common values include `"active"` for usable accounts and possibly more restricted states depending on policy.

ip.description:
Client IP address observed when the admin registration request is performed.

Stored into `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.ip` for the newly created session, enabling future security analysis and anomaly detection. The server may also override or validate this value using its own connection metadata.

href.description:
Full URL (href) of the page or route where the admin registration occurs.

This populates `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.href` for the initial session and provides contextual information for audits about where the session originated.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the previous page or context leading to the admin registration.

Stored into `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.referrer` alongside the new session and used to understand navigation flows and potential security-relevant transitions.

ITodoAppAdminUser.IAuthorized.description:
Response body schema representing a successfully authorized administrative user in the todoApp backend.

This DTO is returned by authentication-related operations such as login and token refresh for the adminUser actor. It encapsulates the stable identity of the admin principal alongside freshly issued JWT tokens that clients use for subsequent administrative API calls.

The schema deliberately exposes only non-sensitive identity fields and token structures. Password hashes, credential internals, and low-level session fields from todo_app_adminusers and todo_app_adminuser_sessions are never included, preserving security and least-privilege principles.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrative user account.

This value corresponds to the primary key id column of the todo_app_adminusers table and is used throughout the system to associate audit records and authorization decisions with a specific admin principal.

Clients may log or cache this identifier for troubleshooting and display purposes, but it must never be treated as a secret.

email.description:
Administrative email address of the authorized user.

This is the same email value stored in the email column of todo_app_adminusers and is typically used as the primary login identifier for administrative access. It helps client applications display who is currently signed in and can be used in UX elements such as headers or audit screens.

The value must be unique among admin accounts and follows standard email formatting rules.

display_name.description:
Optional human-readable display name for the administrative user.

This field corresponds to todo_app_adminusers.display_name and may be null when no friendly name has been configured. When present, it is shown in logs, dashboards, or audit views instead of or in addition to the email address.

status.description:
Operational status of the administrative user account.

This property maps to todo_app_adminusers.status and indicates whether the admin account is currently active and allowed to sign in, or in a restricted state such as 'suspended' or 'disabled'. Business logic interprets the specific string values to enforce access policies.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the administrative user account was created.

This value maps to todo_app_adminusers.created_at and is set once when the row is inserted. It is used for auditing, chronological sorting, and understanding the age of the admin account.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the administrative user account was last updated.

This field reflects the most recent modification to any admin account data in todo_app_adminusers, including changes to email, display_name, status, or password hash. It supports audit trails and helps detect recent administrative changes.

ITodoAppAdminUser.description:
Administrative user DTO representing an operator of the todoApp service.

This type is mapped directly to the todo_app_adminusers Prisma model, which stores administrative users responsible for monitoring and maintaining the todoApp service. It exposes only non-sensitive fields that are safe for API consumers while preserving full lifecycle and status information for each admin account.

The DTO is used as the detailed response type for admin user management endpoints, including read and update operations. It intentionally omits the password_hash column so that password material is never serialized back to clients, while still surfacing identity, display, status, and audit timestamps for administrative workflows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrative user account.

This value maps to todo_app_adminusers.id and is generated as a UUID primary key. It is used in path parameters such as adminUserId for identifying the target admin user in admin management operations.

email.description:
Administrative user email address used as the primary login identifier.

This field maps to todo_app_adminusers.email and is unique among admin users. It is displayed in admin consoles and used when authenticating administrative operators. The value must conform to standard email formatting rules.

display_name.description:
Optional human-readable display name for the administrative user.

This field corresponds to todo_app_adminusers.display_name and may be null when no friendly name has been configured. When present, it is shown in logs, dashboards, or audit views instead of or in addition to the email address.

status.description:
Operational status of the administrative user account.

This property maps to todo_app_adminusers.status and indicates whether the admin account is currently active and allowed to sign in, or in a restricted state such as 'suspended' or 'disabled'. Business logic interprets the specific string values to enforce access policies.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the administrative user account was created.

This value maps to todo_app_adminusers.created_at and is set once when the row is inserted. It is used for auditing, chronological sorting, and understanding the age of the admin account.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the administrative user account was last updated.

This field reflects the most recent modification to any admin account data in todo_app_adminusers, including changes to email, display_name, status, or password hash. It supports audit trails and helps detect recent administrative changes.

ITodoAppAdminUserSession.description:
Detailed representation of a single administrative user authentication session in the todoApp backend.

This DTO mirrors the `todo_app_adminuser_sessions` Prisma model and is used as the response body for inspection-style APIs that allow operators or security tools to review a specific admin session. It exposes identifiers, ownership linkage to the admin account through a summary object, and connection context such as IP and request URLs.

The type is read-only from the API consumer’s perspective and does not provide any mechanism to mutate or revoke the session. Business logic uses this shape to provide a complete, audit-friendly view of when and from where an administrative session was established, as well as whether it has expired.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin user session.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `todo_app_adminuser_sessions` table and is generated by the backend when the session is created. It is used as the stable handle when retrieving session details via administrative APIs.

adminUser.description:
Summary representation of the administrative user who owns this session.

This object corresponds to the admin account referenced by the `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.todo_app_adminuser_id` foreign key and exposes only non-sensitive identity information. It allows audit tools and administrative UIs to understand which admin account is associated with the session without performing an additional lookup.

Using the `.ISummary` variant prevents circular references and keeps the payload lightweight while still providing enough context for investigation and monitoring.

ip.description:
IP address that was observed when this administrative session was initiated.

The value is stored as a textual representation (for example, IPv4 or IPv6 literal) and is captured at login time. It is primarily used for security monitoring, anomaly detection, and incident investigation around administrative access.

href.description:
Full URL (href) that was requested at the moment the admin session was created.

This string preserves the complete entrypoint location, such as the exact page in an administration console where the login or authentication flow began. It is useful for understanding context in forensic reviews and UX analytics.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client when the session was started.

The referrer indicates which page or external site led the administrator into the authentication flow. It provides additional context for tracing navigation paths and analyzing potential security issues such as unexpected origins.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this admin session record was created.

The value reflects the moment at which authentication for the administrative user successfully completed and the session became active. It is stored in a database-compatible date-time format, typically UTC, for consistent auditing and ordering.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the session expired or was explicitly terminated, or null while the session remains active.

When non-null, this value marks the end of the session’s validity for authorization purposes. While the session is still active, the field stays null so that monitoring tools can easily distinguish ongoing sessions from historical ones.

email.description:
Administrative user email address used for login.

This value is matched against the unique, non-nullable `email` column in `todo_app_adminusers` to identify the admin account attempting to authenticate.

password.description:
Plaintext password supplied by the administrative user at login.

The backend hashes this value and compares it to the `password_hash` column in `todo_app_adminusers`. The raw password is never stored and is used only transiently for authentication.

ip.description:
Client IP address at the time of login, if supplied by the caller.

Although the server can derive the IP from the network connection, this optional field allows clients in proxied or SSR environments to pass the original client IP. It will be persisted into the `ip` column of `todo_app_adminuser_sessions` when creating the session.

href.description:
Full URL (current page URL) from which the admin login request was initiated.

This non-nullable value is used to populate the `href` column of `todo_app_adminuser_sessions`, capturing the entry point for the authenticated session to support auditing and security analysis.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page URL) that led to the admin login action.

This value populates the `referrer` column in `todo_app_adminuser_sessions` and records the navigation source or origin that preceded the login page, enabling downstream investigation and behavioral analytics.

ITodoAppAdminUser.ILogin.description:
Login request payload for administrative users of the todoApp service.

This DTO is used by the `/auth/adminUser/login` endpoint to authenticate existing admin accounts stored in the `todo_app_adminusers` table and to create corresponding session rows in `todo_app_adminuser_sessions`. It carries the minimal credential and context information required to verify identity and establish a new authenticated session.

The `email` and `password` fields provide the credentials; the backend derives a secure hash from `password` and compares it to the `password_hash` column for the admin identified by `email`. The `ip`, `href`, and `referrer` properties supply connection context that is persisted to `todo_app_adminuser_sessions` when the session is created. While `ip` is optional and can be inferred from the connection, `href` and `referrer` are required to ensure that every session record has complete entry-point metadata.

No actor identifiers or system-managed fields, such as session IDs or timestamps, are accepted from the client; those are derived and stored exclusively on the server side during the authentication flow.

ITodoAppAdminUser.IRefresh.description:
Request body schema for refreshing administrative JWT tokens for the todoApp service.

This DTO represents the client-provided data required to validate an existing admin session in the todo_app_adminuser_sessions table and to rotate authentication tokens for the associated admin user in todo_app_adminusers.

The structure is intentionally minimal and opaque: it carries a single signed token or session reference string. The server interprets this value to locate and validate a specific todo_app_adminuser_sessions record, verify that it remains time-valid, and confirm that the owning admin account is still in an acceptable status.

No explicit database foreign keys or actor identity fields appear in this schema. All linkage to todo_app_adminuser_sessions and todo_app_adminusers is resolved on the server side using the opaque token value, preserving security by not exposing internal identifiers or session structure details to clients.

refresh_token.description:
Opaque refresh token or signed session reference string used to identify an existing administrative session.

The backend parses and validates this value to locate a todo_app_adminuser_sessions row, typically via a secure lookup keyed by the session's id or a related secret reference. The token may embed cryptographic signatures and expiry information, but these internal details are not visible to clients.

Clients treat this value as an opaque string: they MUST NOT attempt to interpret or modify it. The token is obtained from a previous successful login or refresh response and is required whenever administrative JWT tokens need to be rotated without re-supplying credentials.

ITodoAppSystemSetting.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request body for listing global system configuration entries stored in todo_app_system_settings.

This DTO allows administrative tools to query configuration settings with flexible criteria, including key-based search, grouping, enabled-state filtering, and time range constraints on created_at and updated_at.

It also carries pagination and sorting instructions so that large configuration sets can be browsed efficiently in management consoles and audit interfaces. All filters are optional; when omitted, the server applies sensible defaults and returns a paginated view of all visible settings.

Backends may enforce upper bounds on pageSize and may normalize or validate sortBy and sortDirection values to protect performance and ensure consistent result ordering, even if clients request more aggressive pagination or unsupported sort fields.

page.description:
One-based index of the page of results to return.

If omitted, implementations typically default this value to 1 to return the first page. Combined with pageSize, this controls how many todo_app_system_settings rows are skipped before selecting the current window.

Values less than 1 are considered invalid and should trigger validation errors rather than implicit normalization.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of system setting entries to include in a single page of results.

Administrative frontends use this value to control list density and scrolling behavior. Implementations may enforce an upper bound to prevent excessive result sizes, even if clients request larger values.

When omitted, the backend selects a default size that balances usability and performance for typical system settings volumes. If the client requests a value above the server-side maximum, the backend may clamp it to the allowed limit.

key.description:
Optional exact or partial match filter for the configuration key field.

This value is compared against the key column of todo_app_system_settings to narrow results to entries whose business key matches or contains the supplied text. Implementations may choose between prefix, substring, or exact match semantics depending on UX requirements.

Leaving this field empty or omitting it entirely disables key-based filtering.

group.description:
Optional filter by logical group or category of the setting.

The underlying group column of todo_app_system_settings is used to cluster settings into domains such as "limits", "features", or "experimental". Providing a group value restricts results to entries whose group column matches the given category.

This field is particularly useful for settings management screens that display one domain at a time.

enabled.description:
Optional tri-state filter controlling which enabled states are returned.

When set to true, only settings whose enabled column is true are included. When set to false, only disabled settings are returned. When null or omitted, no filtering by enabled state is applied and both enabled and disabled settings may appear in results.

This allows administrators to quickly focus on currently active configuration entries without losing the ability to review disabled or deprecated settings when needed.

createdFrom.description:
Optional lower bound for the created_at timestamp of returned settings.

When provided, only todo_app_system_settings rows whose created_at value is greater than or equal to this timestamp are included. This helps administrators review recently introduced configuration entries within a specific time window.

The value must be supplied in ISO 8601 date-time format with timezone information.

createdTo.description:
Optional upper bound for the created_at timestamp of returned settings.

When provided, only settings whose created_at value is less than or equal to this timestamp are included. Combined with createdFrom, this supports time range filtering on when configuration entries were first added.

The value uses standard ISO 8601 date-time format including timezone offset or Z-suffix.

updatedFrom.description:
Optional lower bound for the updated_at timestamp of returned settings.

Administrators can use this field to find configuration entries that have been changed recently, by specifying a cutoff date-time and including only rows whose updated_at column is greater than or equal to that value.

The timestamp must be encoded as an ISO 8601 date-time string with timezone information.

updatedTo.description:
Optional upper bound for the updated_at timestamp of returned settings.

Used together with updatedFrom, this allows querying for settings updated within a specific time interval. Only rows whose updated_at value is less than or equal to this timestamp are included.

The string must follow the standard ISO 8601 date-time representation.

sortBy.description:
Optional name of the field used to sort system setting results.

Typical values include "key", "group", "enabled", "created_at", or "updated_at", corresponding to columns in todo_app_system_settings or their logical projections in summary DTOs. Implementations should validate the supplied field name and reject unsupported values.

When omitted, the backend applies a default ordering, such as ascending by key or by group and key combination.

oneOf.description:
Direction in which the results should be sorted.

A value of "asc" requests ascending order, while "desc" requests descending order according to the column indicated by sortBy. If sortBy is omitted, this field may be ignored or applied to a default sort column.

Any value outside the allowed enum is invalid and must be rejected by input validation.
