A value of "asc" requests ascending order, while "desc" requests descending order according to the column indicated by sortBy. If sortBy is omitted, this field may be ignored or applied to a default sort column.

Any value outside the allowed enum is invalid and must be rejected by input validation.

sortDirection.description:
Direction in which the results should be sorted.

A value of "asc" requests ascending order, while "desc" requests descending order according to the column indicated by sortBy. If sortBy is omitted, this field may be ignored or applied to a default sort column.

Any value outside the allowed enum is invalid and must be rejected by input validation.

ITodoAppSystemSetting.description:
Represents a single global configuration or feature flag entry in the todoApp backend.

Each record in this type corresponds directly to a row in the todo_app_system_settings Prisma model, which stores cross-cutting settings that influence behavior of the entire todo service rather than any specific user or todo item. Examples include limits such as the maximum number of active todos per member user, switches to enable or disable optional features, and experimental flags used during gradual rollouts.

The entity includes both business-facing fields like key, value, type, description, and group, and technical lifecycle fields such as enabled, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. Application code typically looks up settings by the unique key, interprets the raw string value according to the type field, and respects the enabled flag and soft-delete semantics indicated by deleted_at when deciding whether to apply a configuration entry.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the system setting record.

This value maps to the id column of the todo_app_system_settings table and is generated as a UUID. It is used internally for database identity and audit purposes rather than as a primary business key in APIs, which rely on the key field instead.

key.description:
Unique business key for the configuration entry.

This field corresponds to the key column in the todo_app_system_settings model and is constrained by a unique index. Application logic and administrative tools use this key, such as "max_active_todos_per_user" or "enable_state_filtering", to look up and manage specific settings.

value.description:
Raw string value of the configuration entry.

The todo_app_system_settings Prisma schema stores all setting values in this string column, while the type field indicates how to interpret the data at runtime. Typical values include numeric limits encoded as decimal strings, boolean flags using values like "true" or "false", and other scalar configuration values.

type.description:
Semantic type descriptor for the configuration value.

This property reflects the type column in todo_app_system_settings and tells the application how to interpret the raw value field. Common examples include markers such as "int", "boolean", "string", or "double". Business logic may validate that value can be parsed into the declared type before applying the setting.

description.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of the configuration entry.

This field mirrors the nullable description column in the todo_app_system_settings Prisma model. It documents the purpose, intended usage, and impact of the setting so that administrators can safely adjust configuration without consulting external documentation.

group.description:
Optional logical group or category label for the configuration entry.

The value corresponds to the nullable group column and is typically used to cluster settings into domains such as "limits", "features", or "experimental" within management UIs. When null, the setting is not assigned to any specific category.

enabled.description:
Indicates whether this configuration entry is currently active.

This property directly maps to the enabled boolean column in todo_app_system_settings. When true, application logic treats the setting as part of the active configuration set. When false, the setting remains stored but may be ignored or overridden by default behavior depending on business rules.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the configuration entry was first created.

This field reflects the non-null created_at column in the todo_app_system_settings table. It records when the setting was initially registered, supporting audit use cases and historical analysis of configuration changes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the configuration entry was last modified.

The value corresponds to the non-null updated_at column and is updated by the system whenever any mutable business field of the setting changes. Administrators can use it to identify recently changed configuration entries and diagnose behavior shifts.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the configuration entry.

This nullable field maps to the deleted_at column in todo_app_system_settings and implements logical removal semantics. When null, the setting is considered part of the live configuration set (subject to enabled). When set to a timestamp, the setting is treated as logically deleted or deprecated while remaining in the database for audit and potential recovery, depending on business policy.

ITodoAppSystemSetting.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new global configuration or feature flag entry in the todoApp backend.

This DTO corresponds to the todo_app_system_settings Prisma model and collects the business fields that an administrative client must provide when registering a new system setting. It excludes system-managed fields such as id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at, which are generated and maintained by the backend, and focuses on semantic configuration information that controls application behavior.

Typical usage includes creating settings like maximum active todo limits, toggles for optional features, and experimental flags. The key must be unique across all settings, the value holds the raw configuration payload as a string, and the type describes how that payload should be interpreted. Optional description and group metadata help operators understand and organize entries, while the enabled flag controls whether the new setting is applied immediately or simply stored in a disabled state for later activation.

key.description:
Unique business key for the new configuration entry.

This property is required on creation and maps to the key column in todo_app_system_settings, which is protected by a unique index. It is the primary identifier used by both application code and administrators to reference this setting, so it should be stable, descriptive, and unique, such as "max_active_todos_per_user".

value.description:
Raw string value to persist for the configuration entry.

On creation, this field provides the initial value for the value column in todo_app_system_settings. The backend will store it as given and later interpret it according to the type field. Examples include numeric values like "1000", boolean flags like "true", or other scalar configuration strings.

type.description:
Semantic type of the configuration value being created.

This property sets the type column in todo_app_system_settings and tells the system how to interpret the associated value at runtime. Typical values include tokens such as "int", "boolean", "string", or "double". Business logic may validate that the provided value is compatible with the declared type before accepting the new setting.

description.description:
Optional human-readable explanation for the new configuration setting.

This field initializes the description column in todo_app_system_settings and should explain what the setting controls, how it affects the todoApp backend, and any caveats administrators should know when adjusting it. When omitted or set to null, the setting will have no descriptive metadata beyond its key.

group.description:
Optional logical group name used to categorize the new setting.

When provided, this value is stored in the group column to cluster related settings into domains such as "limits", "features", or "experimental" in administrative tools. When null, the new entry is not assigned to any specific group.

enabled.description:
Initial enabled state for the new configuration entry.

This flag sets the enabled column of todo_app_system_settings at creation time. When true, the setting becomes active as soon as it is created and may immediately influence backend behavior. When false, the setting is stored but treated as disabled until an administrator explicitly enables it via an update operation.

ITodoAppSystemSetting.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing global configuration entry stored in the todo_app_system_settings Prisma model.

This type is used by the administrative PUT /todoApp/adminUser/systemSettings/{settingKey} endpoint to carry mutable fields for a single system setting. The path parameter settingKey selects the target row by its unique key column, while this DTO provides only the columns that can actually be changed.

System-managed and identity fields such as id, key, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at are intentionally excluded from this schema. The backend is responsible for locating the record by key, applying the requested changes, and refreshing audit timestamps. Business logic must additionally ensure that the combination of type and value remains coherent after the update and that only active (non-soft-deleted) settings are updated.

value.description:
Raw string representation of the configuration value.

This field stores the actual payload for the system setting, such as a numeric limit (for example "10000"), a boolean flag ("true" or "false"), or another scalar value encoded as text. Application logic interprets this string according to the semantic type declared by the type field in the same row.

When updating a setting, clients should provide a value that is compatible with the effective type, and the backend may validate that the string can be parsed safely into the expected runtime type before persisting it.

type.description:
Semantic type of the configuration value stored in value.

Typical values include markers such as "int", "boolean", "string", or "double" that drive how the application converts the raw value string into a strongly typed runtime value. The Prisma model stores this information alongside the value so that multiple logical types can share the same storage column.

During an update, changing the type without adjusting value can cause interpretation mismatches, so the backend may enforce that both are updated together or that the new type remains compatible with the existing value content.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description of the configuration entry.

This text explains the purpose, behavior, and operational impact of the setting so that administrators understand what it controls, such as how it influences todo limits, feature flags, or other cross-cutting behavior.

When null, no additional description is stored and operator tools may fall back to hard-coded documentation or display only the key.

group.description:
Optional logical group or category label for the setting.

Grouping allows administrative tools to cluster settings into domains such as "limits", "features", or "experimental" for easier discovery and management. This value has no direct effect on runtime behavior but improves organization of configuration records.

When null, the setting is treated as ungrouped and may appear in a generic or miscellaneous category in UI listings.

enabled.description:
Indicates whether this configuration entry is currently active.

When true, application code considers the setting when evaluating behavior such as maximum todo counts or conditional feature switches. When false, business logic may ignore the record or fall back to built-in defaults, effectively disabling the configuration without deleting it.

Updates to this flag allow administrators to toggle features or limits on and off quickly while retaining the underlying value and documentation.

ITodoAppGuestUser.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination request DTO for querying conceptual guest user records from the todo_app_guestusers table.

This type is used by the administrative PATCH /todoApp/adminUser/guestUsers endpoint to express flexible filter conditions, sorting preferences, and pagination controls when listing guest user concept rows. Guest users model unauthenticated or anonymous visitors and are primarily used in authorization logic and analytics.

All properties are optional so that administrators can request default listings, constrain results to particular time ranges or external_ref patterns, or adjust page size and sort order. The server must apply sensible defaults for pagination and impose upper bounds on limit to prevent excessively large result sets.

page.description:
1-based page index to retrieve from the guest user search result set.

When omitted, the backend should default to the first page. This value works together with limit to determine which slice of the complete matching dataset is returned in the IPageITodoAppGuestuser.ISummary response.

Values less than 1 should either be normalized to 1 or rejected according to the service's validation policy.

limit.description:
Maximum number of guest user records to include in a single page of results.

Used with the page parameter to control pagination over the todo_app_guestusers table. The server should enforce a sensible upper bound to protect performance and may fall back to a default size if the client does not provide a value.

When combined with filters, this determines how many matching IPageITodoAppGuestuser.ISummary items are returned for the current request.

fromCreatedAt.description:
Optional inclusive lower bound on the created_at timestamp of guest user records.

When provided, only guest users whose created_at is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are eligible for inclusion in the result set. This lets administrators focus on recently created guest concepts or analyze activity starting from a specific point in time.

When null or omitted, no lower time bound is applied based solely on creation time.

toCreatedAt.description:
Optional inclusive upper bound on the created_at timestamp of guest user records.

If set, only guest user rows with created_at less than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are returned. This can be combined with fromCreatedAt to express closed or open-ended time windows for analytics and monitoring.

When null or not provided, the upper bound on creation time is unconstrained and all more recent records may be included subject to other filters.

externalRef.description:
Optional filter on the external_ref column of todo_app_guestusers.

When provided as a non-null string, the backend should match guest concept rows whose external_ref corresponds to the supplied identifier according to the system's chosen comparison strategy (for example exact equality or prefix matching). This allows administrators to correlate specific analytics or tracking IDs with stored guest actors.

When null or omitted, no filter is applied on external_ref and records are selected regardless of whether this column is null or populated.

sortBy.description:
Optional field name that controls the primary sort order of returned guest user records.

Typical values might include "created_at" to order by creation time or "id" to provide a stable but implementation-oriented ordering. The service should validate this value against a whitelist of supported sort keys and fall back to a default when omitted or invalid.

When null, the backend applies its default ordering, which is commonly descending by created_at so that the newest guest entries appear first.

sortDirection.description:
Optional sort direction applied in combination with sortBy.

Expected values are logical markers such as "asc" for ascending order or "desc" for descending order. The server must validate this value and choose a default, typically descending, when the client either omits the field or supplies an unsupported direction.

This setting, together with sortBy, determines how guest user summary rows are ordered in the paginated IPageITodoAppGuestuser.ISummary response.

ITodoAppGuestUser.description:
Guest user concept representation as an API DTO for the todoApp service.

This type maps directly to the `todo_app_guestusers` Prisma model, which represents the conceptual "guestUser" actor used in authorization logic and analytics for unauthenticated visitors. Each record corresponds to a transient or anonymous visitor rather than an authenticated account.

The DTO exposes the primary key identifier, optional external reference used for correlation with external systems or analytics, and auditing timestamps used for retention and diagnostic purposes.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user concept record.

This field maps to the `id` primary key column of the `todo_app_guestusers` table and is a UUID value used to distinguish guest records for internal diagnostics and analytics.

It is generated by the system and is always present for any persisted guest user concept row.

external_ref.description:
Optional external correlation reference for this guest concept.

This field maps to the nullable `external_ref` column in the `todo_app_guestusers` table. It may contain an external tracking identifier, analytics correlation key, or another non-PII token used to link guest interactions across systems.

When no persistent guest identity is required, this field is stored as null and omitted from correlation workflows.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the guest user concept record.

This field maps to the non-null `created_at` column in the `todo_app_guestusers` schema and records when the guest concept entry was first created in the system.

It is used for audit trails, retention policy enforcement, and chronological reporting of guest activity initialization.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the guest user concept record.

This field maps to the non-null `updated_at` column in the `todo_app_guestusers` table and is refreshed whenever metadata for the guest concept is modified.

It enables tracking of the most recent time the guest-related data was touched for maintenance, analytics corrections, or other operational purposes.

ITodoAppMemberUser.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination request DTO for querying member users in the todoApp service.

This type is used as the request body for administrative search operations targeting the `todo_app_memberusers` Prisma model, which stores authenticated member user accounts that own personal todos. It does not map 1:1 to a single database row, but instead encapsulates query parameters that control which member accounts are returned.

Consumers of this schema can combine free-text search, status-based filters, creation date ranges, and pagination controls to implement powerful administrative user management views without exposing internal implementation details of the member user table.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated member user search results.

This value controls which page of the filtered result set is returned. A value of 1 refers to the first page. Administrative clients can increment this value to fetch subsequent pages when browsing large member user populations.

If omitted, the backend should default to the first page according to its own configuration.

limit.description:
Maximum number of member user records to return in a single page.

This field defines the page size for the search result set. Typical values are in the range of 10–100 depending on UI requirements. The backend may enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses.

If not provided, a sensible default page size configured by the system will be applied.

search.description:
Free-text search term applied to member user identity fields.

This value is typically matched against fields such as `email` or `display_name` from the `todo_app_memberusers` table to support quick lookup of specific accounts. Implementations may apply case-insensitive and partial matching rules.

When omitted or empty, no free-text search filter is applied and only structured filters such as status or date range will affect the result set.

status.description:
Optional status filter limiting results to member accounts in a particular lifecycle state.

This value corresponds to the `status` column of the `todo_app_memberusers` schema, whose documentation mentions common business statuses such as `active`, `blocked`, or `disabled`. Administrative tools can use this filter to focus on problematic accounts or specific lifecycle stages.

If not provided, results may include member users of all statuses subject to other filters.

created_from.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the `created_at` timestamp of member user accounts.

When provided, only member users whose `created_at` column is on or after this ISO 8601 timestamp are eligible to appear in the result set. This allows administrators to constrain searches to accounts created during a particular reporting period.

If omitted, no lower bound is enforced on creation time beyond any implicit retention rules.

created_to.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the `created_at` timestamp of member user accounts.

When provided together with or without `created_from`, this value restricts results to member users created on or before the given ISO 8601 timestamp. It enables reporting and audit views over a fixed time window.

If not specified, no explicit upper bound on creation time is applied aside from the current time.

order_by.description:
Field name used to sort the member user search results.

Typical values include `created_at` to sort by account creation time or `status` to group accounts by lifecycle state. The actual set of supported fields should correspond to indexed columns in the `todo_app_memberusers` table, such as `status` and `created_at`.

If omitted, the backend may default to ordering by `created_at` descending so that the newest accounts appear first.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction for the `order_by` field in member user search results.

Common values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When combined with `order_by = created_at`, this allows administrators to switch between oldest-first and newest-first views.

If not supplied, the service may default to descending order to surface the most recent accounts at the top.

ITodoAppMemberUser.description:
Represents an authenticated member user account within the TodoApp service.

This DTO is a detailed view mapped directly from the todo_app_memberusers Prisma model and is used in administrative read operations such as inspecting, updating, or erasing member user records.

The type exposes core identity and profile fields such as the primary identifier, email, optional display name, current business status, and lifecycle timestamps.

It is intended primarily for backoffice or internal tools rather than public self-service APIs and therefore can safely include operational fields that administrators need to see while still excluding sensitive authentication artifacts like raw passwords.

Each instance corresponds to exactly one row in the todo_app_memberusers table and reflects the latest persisted state, including changes applied through ITodoAppMemberUser.IUpdate and ITodoAppMemberuserStatus.IUpdate operations.

id.description:
Primary key of the member user account.

This value directly corresponds to the id column in the todo_app_memberusers Prisma model and uniquely identifies a single member user within the TodoApp system.

It is generated and managed by the backend and is required when addressing a specific member user in administrative operations such as GET, PUT, or DELETE on /todoApp/adminUser/memberUsers/{memberUserId}.

email.description:
Login and contact email address for the member user.

This field maps to the email column on the todo_app_memberusers table and must be unique across all member users, as enforced by a unique index.

It serves both as the primary authentication identifier and as a primary communication channel for notifications or account-related messages.

display_name.description:
Optional human-friendly name or nickname used in administrative and user interfaces.

This property maps to the nullable display_name column in the todo_app_memberusers Prisma model and may be null when the user has not provided a separate display label.

When present, it is typically used for more readable displays in management consoles and reports instead of showing only the raw email address.

status.description:
Business status of the member user account.

This field corresponds to the non-null status column on todo_app_memberusers and is used to control whether the member is allowed to perform todo operations.

Typical values include states such as "active", "blocked", or "disabled", and administrative status update endpoints (for example, PUT /todoApp/adminUser/memberUsers/{memberUserId}/status) modify this value according to business rules.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the member user account record was created.

This property mirrors the created_at column on the todo_app_memberusers Prisma model and is set once at insertion time.

Administrators and support tools can use it for audit purposes, ordering accounts chronologically, or identifying legacy users.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp describing the last time the member user account data was modified.

It maps to the updated_at column in todo_app_memberusers and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable fields such as email, display_name, or status are changed.

This value allows operators to track recent account activity and to verify that update operations have been applied as expected.

ITodoAppMemberUser.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating mutable attributes of a TodoApp member user account.

This type is used as the request body schema for administrative update operations on the todo_app_memberusers table, such as PUT /todoApp/adminUser/memberUsers/{memberUserId}.

It exposes only those columns that are considered safe and meaningful to change after account creation, for example profile-related fields and selected business flags, while omitting immutable identifiers and system-managed values.

System fields such as id, created_at, and updated_at, as well as sensitive authentication artifacts including password_hash, are intentionally excluded to preserve data integrity and to keep authentication concerns delegated to dedicated subsystems.

All properties are optional so that callers can perform partial updates, sending only the fields they intend to modify.

email.description:
New email address for the member user, if it needs to be changed.

When provided, this value updates the email column on the todo_app_memberusers model and must remain unique across all member users due to the database-level unique constraint.

Because the email is also used as the login identifier, administrative tools should apply appropriate validation and confirmation flows when modifying this field.

display_name.description:
Updated human-friendly display name or nickname for the member user.

Supplying a non-null string will set or replace the existing display_name value on the todo_app_memberusers row, while explicitly sending null will clear any previously stored nickname.

This field is optional and may be omitted from the payload when the display name should remain unchanged.

status.description:
Updated business status for the member user account.

Although there is a dedicated status-specific endpoint, this field may be included when an administrative update operation is designed to allow changing status alongside other profile fields.

Any supplied value must conform to the allowed set of status strings configured for todo_app_memberusers (for example, "active", "blocked", or "disabled"), and the backend should enforce valid transitions according to business rules.

ITodoAppMemberUserSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering DTO for listing authentication sessions of a specific member user in the todoApp service.

This schema encapsulates pagination, sorting, and optional filter criteria used when querying the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` Prisma model for a particular member user. It is consumed by the administrative list endpoint that operates on the `/memberUsers/{memberUserId}/sessions` path and always scopes results to the member identified by the path parameter.

The request object is deliberately simple and focuses on generic list controls that are stable across implementations. Domain-specific filters such as IP address or date ranges can be added in future variants if needed, but the core contract provides predictable pagination behavior for administrative consoles and monitoring tools.

page.description:
1-based page index indicating which slice of the member user's session list to retrieve.

Clients should start with page value `1` for the first page and increment it to traverse subsequent pages. The backend uses this index together with the `limit` field to compute the offset when querying the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` table for the target member user.

If omitted, implementations typically default this value to `1`, returning the first page of results.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return in a single page of results.

This value is used in combination with the `page` parameter to control pagination over the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` table for the specified member user. Reasonable values typically range from 10 to 100, and servers may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default page size that balances usability and system load.

orderBy.description:
Optional sort key indicating which field of the session records should be used for ordering.

Common values include `created_at` to sort sessions by their creation time or `expired_at` to group active and expired sessions. When not provided, servers usually default to descending `created_at` so the most recent sessions appear first.

The backend should validate this value against a whitelist of supported sort columns to prevent misuse or invalid field names.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the chosen `orderBy` field when ordering session records.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, implementations usually default to `desc` so that the most recent or most significant sessions appear first in the list.

Clients should treat this as a small controlled vocabulary and avoid sending arbitrary strings; servers may normalize case and reject unsupported values.

ITodoAppMemberUserSession.description:
Detailed view of a single authentication session belonging to a specific member user in the todoApp service.

This DTO is used primarily by administrative tooling to inspect security-relevant information about when and how a member user session was established, without exposing any sensitive authentication secrets. It mirrors the structure of the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` Prisma model and includes contextual information about the owning member user through a summary reference.

The type is returned by administrative endpoints that retrieve or inspect sessions and is never used directly as a request body. It provides all lifecycle timestamps of the session and basic connection metadata such as IP address and entrypoint URLs so that operators can perform audits and investigations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member user session.

This value corresponds directly to the primary key of the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` table and is generated by the authentication subsystem when the session is created. It is used to reference this session in administrative APIs and logging systems.

memberUser.description:
Summary information about the member user who owns this session.

This reference is derived from the `todo_app_memberuser_id` foreign key of the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` table and provides enough information to identify the account involved in the session without embedding the full member user entity.

ip.description:
IP address from which this session was established.

The value is stored in the `ip` column of `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and represents the client IP captured at login time. It is used for security analysis and anomaly detection routines.

href.description:
Full URL (href) requested when the session was created.

This value comes from the `href` column of `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and indicates the entrypoint within the todoApp frontend where the authentication occurred. Operators can use it to understand which part of the application initiated the session.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client when the session started.

It maps to the `referrer` field in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and describes the previous page or origin that led to the login request. This supports navigation and origin analysis when investigating login patterns.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the session record was created.

This field mirrors the `created_at` column in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and marks the moment when the authentication succeeded and the session became active.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session expired or was explicitly terminated, if applicable.

This corresponds to the `expired_at` column in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions`. While null, the session is treated as active; when set, it indicates the point in time after which the session is no longer valid.

ITodoAppMemberUser.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an authenticated member user of the todoApp service.

This type is optimized for list views, references from other entities, and any context where a compact representation of a member account is sufficient.

It exposes only non-sensitive identification and status fields, ensuring that authentication secrets such as password hashes are never leaked into API responses.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member user account.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `todo_app_memberusers` table and is used to join todos and other member-owned resources.

email.description:
Member user email address used as the primary login identifier and for communication.

The value is unique across all member users and is safe to expose in summary views for administrative tooling and owner-facing UIs.

display_name.description:
Optional human-friendly name or nickname displayed in user interfaces.

When null, client applications can fall back to the email address or another derived label when showing member information.

status.description:
Business status of the member account.

Typical values include `active`, `blocked`, or `disabled`, and they determine whether the member is allowed to perform todo operations. Exact allowed values are enforced at the service layer according to business rules.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the member user account was created.

Commonly used for auditing, ordering lists of users, and analytics such as cohort calculations.

ITodoAppAdminUser.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for querying TodoApp administrative users with pagination support.

This DTO is used as the request body for the `PATCH /todoApp/adminUser/adminUsers` operation to submit complex search criteria that cannot be represented conveniently as simple query parameters. It allows the caller to constrain which admin user records from `todo_app_adminusers` should be returned in a paginated result set.

Fields in this type are all optional filters or pagination directives. When omitted, the corresponding constraint is not applied and default pagination settings may be used. The structure is designed for administrative tooling and should be interpreted together with the response type `IPageITodoAppAdminuser.ISummary`.

page.description:
Requested page index for paginated results.

This is a 1-based page number indicating which slice of the admin user list should be returned. When omitted, the backend should default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of admin user records to include in a single page.

If not provided, the system applies a sensible default and may also enforce an upper bound to protect performance. This value controls the size of the `data` array in the paginated response.

email.description:
Optional email filter for administrative users.

When provided, this value is used to restrict results from `todo_app_adminusers` to records whose `email` matches or partially matches the given text, depending on implementation. It helps quickly locate admins by their login email.

status.description:
Optional status filter for administrative users.

This value is compared to the `status` column of `todo_app_adminusers` (for example `active`, `suspended`, or `disabled`) to restrict results to accounts in a specific operational state.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for ordering administrative users by their `created_at` timestamp.

Use `asc` to list older admin accounts first and `desc` to list the most recently created accounts first. When omitted, the backend may apply a default ordering strategy.

Sort direction for ordering administrative users by their `created_at` timestamp.

Use `asc` to list older admin accounts first and `desc` to list the most recently created accounts first. When omitted, the backend may apply a default ordering strategy.

orderByCreatedAt.description:
Sort direction for ordering administrative users by their `created_at` timestamp.

Use `asc` to list older admin accounts first and `desc` to list the most recently created accounts first. When omitted, the backend may apply a default ordering strategy.

createdFrom.description:
Lower bound of the admin account creation timestamp filter.

When provided, only admin user records with `created_at` greater than or equal to this value in the `todo_app_adminusers` table should be included in the search results. This is useful for focusing on accounts created after a specific point in time.

createdTo.description:
Upper bound of the admin account creation timestamp filter.

When provided, only admin user records with `created_at` less than or equal to this value in the `todo_app_adminusers` table should be included in the search results. This is useful for limiting results to accounts created up to a specific point in time.

ITodoAppAdminUser.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an administrative user account for the todoApp backend.

This DTO is used in administrative consoles, logs, and references where a compact view of the admin identity is sufficient. It deliberately excludes sensitive authentication information such as password hashes while exposing key identity, status, and lifecycle data for oversight and auditing.

Because admin accounts are security-sensitive, this summary is suitable only for trusted internal contexts and should not be exposed to unprivileged client applications.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin user account.

This maps to the primary key `id` of the `todo_app_adminusers` table and serves as the stable technical identifier for administrative operations and audit logs.

email.description:
Email address used as the primary login identifier for the admin account.

This reflects the `email` column in `todo_app_adminusers`, which is constrained to be unique among admin users and is the main contact point for administrative notifications.

display_name.description:
Optional human-readable name for the admin user.

This value corresponds to the nullable `display_name` column in `todo_app_adminusers` and is typically shown in dashboards, logs, and activity traces instead of the raw email when available.

status.description:
Operational status of the admin account, such as `active`, `suspended`, or `disabled`.

This maps directly to the `status` column in `todo_app_adminusers` and determines whether the admin can sign in and perform privileged operations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin user account was created.

This corresponds to the `created_at` column in `todo_app_adminusers` and is useful for auditing, accountability, and tracking onboarding of administrative staff.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating the most recent update to the admin user account record.

This field maps to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in the `todo_app_adminusers` Prisma model and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable attributes of the admin account are changed. It is commonly used in administrative consoles and audit logs to understand when account details, such as status or display name, were last modified.

ITodoAppAdminUser.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying non-sensitive fields of an administrative user account.

This type is used as the request body for PUT /todoApp/adminUser/adminUsers/{adminUserId}, where the adminUserId path parameter specifies which todo_app_adminusers row to update. It carries only fields that are allowed to be changed via the general update operation.

The DTO never includes identity, ownership, or system-managed fields such as id, created_at, or updated_at, and it does not expose or accept raw password_hash values. Instead it focuses on editable business attributes like email, display_name, and status, allowing partial updates where any subset of those fields may be supplied.

email.description:
New email address for the administrative user account.

When provided, this value updates todo_app_adminusers.email and must remain unique among admin users. It continues to act as the primary login identifier for the admin account. If omitted, the existing email remains unchanged.

display_name.description:
New display name for the administrative user account.

This property updates todo_app_adminusers.display_name. Supplying a non-null string sets or replaces the friendly name shown in admin consoles, while explicitly passing null clears any previously stored display name. When omitted, the current value is preserved.

status.description:
New operational status for the administrative user account.

This field updates todo_app_adminusers.status when included. It should be set to one of the allowed status values such as 'active', 'suspended', or 'disabled' according to business validation. When not provided, the existing status is left untouched.

ITodoAppAdminUser.IUpdateStatus.description:
DTO for updating the operational status of an administrative user account in the todoApp backend.

This type is used exclusively by the status update endpoint, which changes the `status` column in the `todo_app_adminusers` Prisma model while refreshing the `updated_at` timestamp. It does not allow modification of identity or credential fields such as `email` or `password_hash`.

The DTO focuses on carrying the new status value and, optionally, a free-form reason string that can be stored in logs or used by higher layers for audit trails. Actual persistence of the reason text is implementation-specific and may be handled outside the core admin user table.

status.description:
New operational status for the administrative user account.

This value is written to the `status` column of the `todo_app_adminusers` table, which represents the lifecycle state of the admin account (for example, `active`, `suspended`, or `disabled`).

Implementations must validate this field against the allowed status set defined in business rules and may reject transitions that violate policy (such as reactivating permanently disabled accounts).

reason.description:
Optional human-readable explanation describing why the admin account status is being changed.

Typical examples include security incident investigation, policy enforcement, or routine administrative maintenance. This field is intended primarily for audit logging or UI display and is not persisted in the `todo_app_adminusers` table itself unless explicitly modeled elsewhere.

oneOf.description:
Represents an administrative actor in the todoApp unified authentication layer.

This value indicates that the underlying principal is backed by a row in the `todo_app_adminusers` table and has elevated operational capabilities for managing the service.

Represents a member user actor in the todoApp unified authentication layer.

This value indicates that the underlying principal is backed by a row in the `todo_app_memberusers` table and owns personal todos within the service.

Represents a guest user actor in the todoApp unified authentication layer.

This value indicates that the underlying principal corresponds to a conceptual guest record in the `todo_app_guestusers` table, typically used for anonymous or unauthenticated interactions.

IETodoAppActorKind.description:
Enumeration of actor kinds supported by the todoApp unified authentication layer.

This enum distinguishes which concrete actor implementation underlies the currently authenticated principal, such as an administrative user, a member user who owns todos, or a conceptual guest representation. It allows clients to branch logic and render appropriate UI depending on the actor type.

Typical values align with the main actor tables: `adminUser` for rows in `todo_app_adminusers`, `memberUser` for rows in `todo_app_memberusers`, and `guestUser` for records in `todo_app_guestusers`. Additional values can be introduced as the service evolves.

ITodoAppActorCurrent.description:
Unified representation of the actor currently authenticated in the todoApp service.

This DTO does not map directly to a single Prisma table; instead it aggregates identity and role information derived from the active security context, which may point to an admin user, member user, or guest user record. It is returned by the `/todoApp/memberUser/actors/current` endpoint so that clients can bootstrap their state after authentication without knowing underlying table structures.

The structure exposes which actor kind is active and provides exactly one non-null summary object for the concrete actor implementation (for example an admin summary when the actorKind is `adminUser`). It intentionally excludes sensitive authentication material such as password hashes, and it relies on session or token mechanisms for actual authentication state.

actorKind.description:
Kind of actor that is currently authenticated.

This value tells the client whether the authenticated principal is an administrative user, a member user, or a guest. It is used to branch UI flows and authorization checks, and it corresponds to one of the concrete summary objects embedded in this DTO.

adminUser.description:
Administrative user summary when the current actor is an admin, or null otherwise.

When `actorKind` is `adminUser`, this property contains a populated `ITodoAppAdminUser.ISummary` object summarizing the admin account associated with the current session or token. For other actor kinds it will be null so that clients do not need to guess which summary is relevant.

memberUser.description:
Member user summary when the current actor is an authenticated member, or null otherwise.

If `actorKind` is `memberUser`, this property contains a lightweight view of the owning member account from `todo_app_memberusers`. It remains null for admin or guest sessions, ensuring only one concrete actor summary is populated at a time.

guestUser.description:
Guest user summary when the current actor corresponds to a guest concept, or null otherwise.

For sessions or tokens that represent guests rather than authenticated accounts, this property carries a summary of the relevant `todo_app_guestusers` record if one exists. In all other actor modes the value is null and should be ignored by clients.

ITodoAppSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request for listing authentication sessions of the current actor in the TodoApp service.

This DTO is used by the PATCH /todoApp/memberUser/actors/current/sessions endpoint to express complex search criteria and pagination options for sessions backed by the todo_app_memberuser_sessions and todo_app_adminuser_sessions tables. It never carries any actor identity because the current member or admin is resolved from authentication context.

The properties focus on pagination controls and optional filters such as IP address and time ranges for creation and expiry. All filters are optional so that clients can request the default view by omitting them, while still having the ability to narrow results when needed.

page.description:
Zero-based page index for pagination.

This value selects which slice of the result set to return when combined with the limit property. Page 0 corresponds to the first page of results. If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default, typically the first page.

Clients should treat this as a non-negative integer. Values less than 0 are considered invalid and will result in a validation error.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return in a single page.

This value controls the page size for the paginated session list. When not provided, the server uses a default limit that balances responsiveness and payload size. Excessively large values may be clamped to a server-defined maximum to protect performance.

Clients should use moderate values to keep responses efficient while minimizing the number of round trips needed to navigate all sessions.

ip.description:
Optional filter for the client IP address associated with sessions.

When provided, the backend narrows results to sessions whose stored ip column matches the specified value, typically using an exact match. This helps users inspect where they have signed in from a particular address.

Use null or omit the property to avoid filtering on IP and return sessions regardless of their originating address.

createdFrom.description:
Lower bound of the session creation time range filter.

When specified, only sessions whose created_at timestamp is greater than or equal to this value are included in the result set. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string.

Set to null or omit the property to avoid constraining the lower bound of creation time.

createdTo.description:
Upper bound of the session creation time range filter.

When provided, only sessions whose created_at timestamp is less than or equal to this value are returned. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string.

Set to null or omit the property to disable the upper bound filter on creation time.

expiredFrom.description:
Lower bound of the session expiry time range filter.

When provided, this constraint selects sessions where the expired_at timestamp is greater than or equal to the given date-time, allowing clients to focus on sessions that expired after a certain moment.

Set to null or omit the property to avoid filtering by the lower bound of expiry time.

expiredTo.description:
Upper bound of the session expiry time range filter.

When specified, only sessions whose expired_at timestamp is less than or equal to this date-time are included. This can be used together with expiredFrom to isolate sessions that ended within a particular window.

Set to null or omit the property to disable the upper bound filter on expiry time.

activeOnly.description:
Flag indicating whether to restrict the result to currently active sessions only.

When true, the backend returns only sessions that are considered active, typically those where expired_at is null or in the future according to business rules. When false or null, both active and historical sessions may be included, depending on other filters.

Use this flag to implement views such as "currently active logins" where the user wants to see only sessions that have not yet expired.

ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request for listing todo items owned by the current member user in the TodoApp service.

This DTO is used by the PATCH /todoApp/memberUser/todos endpoint to express rich filtering, sorting, and pagination over the todo_app_todos table. It never contains the member user identifier because ownership is always derived from the authenticated actor context.

Clients can use the properties to narrow the result set by text search, lifecycle state, and key timestamps, while also controlling page size and index for list views such as "My todos" or "Completed todos".

page.description:
Zero-based page index for paginating todo results.

This integer selects which page of todos to return when used together with the limit property. Page 0 represents the first page. Negative values are invalid and will result in request rejection.

If omitted, the backend applies a default page index, typically 0, to return the first slice of results.

limit.description:
Maximum number of todo summaries to include in a single response page.

This parameter controls the page size and directly affects response payload size and the number of round trips needed to browse all todos. Very large limits may be capped by the server to protect performance.

When not provided, the server uses a default limit appropriate for common list views.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to the todo title or description.

When supplied, the implementation typically performs a case-insensitive search over the title column, and may also search the description field depending on configuration. This allows users to quickly find todos containing particular words or phrases.

Set to null or omit this property to disable text search and return todos based solely on other filters and pagination.

state.description:
Optional filter for the lifecycle state of the todo.

Allowed values correspond to the business meanings of the state column in todo_app_todos, such as "active" or "completed". When provided, only todos in the specified state are included in the result set.

Set to null or omit this property to include todos regardless of state, apart from any implicit exclusion of soft-deleted rows where deleted_at is non-null.

createdFrom.description:
Lower bound of the creation time range filter.

Todos whose created_at timestamp is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are eligible to appear in the result set. This is useful for listing todos created after a specific date.

Set to null or omit the property to avoid constraining the lower bound of creation time.

createdTo.description:
Upper bound of the creation time range filter.

Only todos whose created_at timestamp is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are returned when the filter is set. Combined with createdFrom, this allows clients to restrict results to a specific creation window.

Set to null or omit the property to disable the upper bound filter on creation time.

dueFrom.description:
Lower bound of the due date range filter.

Todos with a due_date greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are considered in the result set when this filter is provided. This enables views for todos due after a specific date.

Set to null or omit the property to avoid filtering by the lower bound of due date.

dueTo.description:
Upper bound of the due date range filter.

When provided, only todos whose due_date is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are returned. Combined with dueFrom, this allows users to see todos due within a defined window.

Set to null or omit the property to disable the upper bound filter on due date.

completed.description:
Optional boolean flag indicating whether to restrict results to completed or non-completed todos.

When true, the backend returns only todos that are considered completed, typically those with a non-null completed_at timestamp and a suitable state value. When false, only todos that are not yet completed are included.

Set to null or omit this property to return todos regardless of completion status, subject to any explicit state filter specified in the request.

ITodoAppTodo.description:
Todo item entity representing a single personal task owned by a member user.

Each instance of this type maps directly to a row in the todo_app_todos table and models the minimal yet complete state of a todo in the todoApp service. It includes identifiers, ownership reference to the member user, core content fields, lifecycle state, and key timestamps that drive ordering and business rules.

This representation is used in detailed responses where a client needs to see the full persisted state of a todo, such as after creation, update, or when fetching an individual todo item.

id.description:
Primary identifier of the todo item.

This field maps to todo_app_todos.id and uniquely distinguishes each todo record within the system. It is generated by the backend and never provided by clients in request bodies.

memberUser.description:
Owner of this todo item as a summarized member user resource.

This object reflects the member account from todo_app_memberusers that created and manages the todo. It replaces the underlying foreign key todo_app_memberuser_id to provide richer context to clients without exposing raw foreign key fields.

title.description:
Short human-readable title of the todo.

This value maps to todo_app_todos.title and must be non-empty text summarizing the work to be done. Clients use it as the primary visible label when listing or displaying todos.

description.description:
Optional extended free-text description for the todo.

This field corresponds to todo_app_todos.description and can be null when no additional detail is supplied. It is used to store longer explanations or notes related to the task.

state.description:
Business state of the todo item.

This property maps to todo_app_todos.state and indicates whether the todo is currently active, completed, or treated as removed through soft deletion logic. Typical conceptual values include "active" (or "pending") and "completed". Application logic uses this state for filtering and lifecycle enforcement.

due_date.description:
Optional target date and time by which the user intends to complete the todo.

This maps to todo_app_todos.due_date and is null when the todo has no explicit due date. When present, it is represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp for the todo item.

This field corresponds to todo_app_todos.created_at and records when the todo was first inserted. It is immutable after creation and is often used for chronological ordering in client views.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the todo item.

This value maps to todo_app_todos.updated_at and is refreshed whenever the todo content, state, or due date changes. Clients can use it to detect recently modified items.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo was most recently marked as completed.

This property corresponds to todo_app_todos.completed_at. It is null when the todo has never been completed or has been reopened without being completed again.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp of the todo item.

This maps to todo_app_todos.deleted_at and is null while the todo is visible in normal lists. When set, the todo is considered logically deleted and typically excluded from member-facing queries.

ITodoAppTodo.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new personal todo item for the authenticated member user.

This type represents the client-supplied attributes required to insert a new row into the `todo_app_todos` Prisma model, excluding server-managed fields such as the primary key, ownership foreign key, and audit timestamps. It is used as the request body for the POST `/todoApp/memberUser/todos` operation.

The backend derives the owning member user from the authenticated session and fills fields like `id`, `todo_app_memberuser_id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` automatically. Business rules for todo content and lifecycle, including required text and optional due date, are enforced against this DTO before persistence.

title.description:
Short human-readable title of the new todo.

Clients must provide a non-empty string that summarizes the task. This value is mapped to the `title` column in `todo_app_todos` and is required for every new todo item.

description.description:
Optional longer free-text description for the new todo.

When provided, this text is stored in the `description` column of `todo_app_todos` and can be used to capture detailed instructions or notes. Clients may send null to omit additional detail.

due_date.description:
Optional target date and time when the user intends to complete the todo.

If supplied, the value is stored in the `due_date` column of `todo_app_todos` and must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string. When null, the todo is created without an explicit due date.

state.description:
Initial business state of the todo.

This value initializes the `state` column in `todo_app_todos` and should reflect an allowed starting status such as active or pending. The backend may override or validate this against lifecycle rules to prevent invalid initial states.

ITodoAppTodo.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing todo item owned by a member user.

This DTO maps to the `todo_app_todos` Prisma model and is consumed by the PUT `/todoApp/memberUser/todos/{todoId}` endpoint to modify mutable fields of an existing todo record. It intentionally omits system-managed identifiers and ownership fields such as `id`, `todo_app_memberuser_id`, and all audit timestamps, so clients must never attempt to send or override those values.

All properties in this update DTO are optional, enabling true partial updates where callers send only the fields they intend to change. Business logic applies todo lifecycle rules when interpreting changes to `state` and `due_date`, and it enforces ownership by combining the authenticated member user with the `todoId` path parameter. Some lifecycle transitions, such as completing or reopening todos, are typically exposed through dedicated endpoints and may be rejected here if they conflict with those rules.

title.description:
New title for the todo item.

This value maps directly to the `todo_app_todos.title` column when provided. It should remain a concise, human-readable summary of the task, and server-side validation is expected to reject empty or whitespace-only titles so that todos always have a meaningful label.

description.description:
New extended description for the todo.

When supplied as a non-null string, this value replaces the existing `todo_app_todos.description` content and can hold a longer free-text explanation of the task. When explicitly set to `null`, it clears any existing description in the database. If the property is omitted from the request body, the current description value remains unchanged.

state.description:
Updated business state of the todo.

This property maps to the `todo_app_todos.state` column when present. Valid values are constrained by the todo lifecycle (for example, conceptual states such as "active" or "completed"), even though the JSON type is a free-form string. Application logic enforces which transitions are allowed here and may require certain state changes—such as completion or reopening—to be performed via dedicated action endpoints like `/complete` or `/reopen` instead of direct updates.

due_date.description:
Updated due date and time for the todo.

When provided as a date-time string, this value updates the `todo_app_todos.due_date` column and must follow the ISO 8601 `date-time` format in UTC. Supplying `null` explicitly clears any existing due date so the todo no longer has a scheduled target time. If the property is omitted entirely, the stored due date value is left unchanged.

ITodoAppSystemSetting.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a global system setting controlling todoApp behavior.

This type maps to the `todo_app_system_settings` Prisma model and is designed for list and lightweight display contexts, such as administrative UIs that show available configuration entries. It surfaces the identifying key, semantic type, raw value, and core metadata needed to understand and manage configuration without loading every column from the underlying table.

Timestamps and soft-deletion metadata (such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at`) are intentionally omitted to keep the payload compact for summary views. When operators require full historical or auditing detail for a specific setting, they are expected to use a more detailed DTO that exposes every column of the configuration record.

id.description:
Primary identifier of the system setting record.

This field corresponds to `todo_app_system_settings.id` and uniquely identifies a particular configuration entry within the todoApp backend. It is used by administrative operations to address a specific setting row when reading or modifying configuration.

key.description:
Business key used to look up this setting in application logic.

This property maps to `todo_app_system_settings.key` and is unique across all settings. Typical examples include names such as `"max_active_todos_per_user"` or `"enable_state_filtering"`, which are consumed by backend services to drive conditional behavior.

value.description:
Raw configuration value stored for this setting.

This field reflects `todo_app_system_settings.value` and is always persisted as a string, regardless of the semantic type. Application code interprets this text according to the associated `type` field, for example parsing it as an integer limit, a boolean flag, or another scalar value.

type.description:
Semantic type describing how to interpret the `value` field.

This property maps to `todo_app_system_settings.type` and normally holds indicators such as `"int"`, `"boolean"`, or `"string"`. It allows business logic and administrative tools to parse, validate, and render the `value` safely and consistently.

description.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of what this setting controls.

This field corresponds to `todo_app_system_settings.description` and helps operators understand the purpose, usage, and impact of the configuration entry when administering the service. It may be null when no explicit documentation has been provided for the setting.

group.description:
Optional logical group or category name for the setting.

This property maps to `todo_app_system_settings.group` and can be used to cluster settings into domains such as "limits", "features", or "experimental". Administrative UIs typically use this to organize configuration lists and filters.

enabled.description:
Indicates whether this setting is currently active.

This field corresponds to `todo_app_system_settings.enabled`. When `true`, the setting is considered in effect and may override built-in defaults. When `false`, application logic may ignore the configuration row or fall back to default behavior while still retaining the record for future reactivation or auditing.

ITodoAppMemberUserSession.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a member user session in the todoApp service.

This summary is intended for list and reference views where only high‑level session information is needed, not full authentication or security details.

It focuses on identifying the session, associating it with its owning member user, and exposing core lifecycle timestamps and connection context for observability and audit UIs.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member user session.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` table and uniquely distinguishes a single authenticated session record.

memberUser.description:
Summary information about the member user who owns this session.

This object is derived from the `todo_app_memberusers` model and allows UIs to show who the session belongs to without exposing sensitive account details.

ip.description:
IP address from which this session was established.

The value comes from the `ip` column of the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` table and is used primarily for security analysis, anomaly detection, and audit trails.

href.description:
Full URL (href) that was requested when the session was created.

This originates from the `href` column in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and provides contextual information about the entry point used when the member logged in.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL recorded when the session started.

This mirrors the `referrer` column in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and helps understand how the user navigated into the application at the time of login.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the session was created.

This maps directly to the `created_at` column in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and represents the start time of authenticated access for this session.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the session expired or was explicitly terminated, or null while the session is still active.

This value corresponds to the nullable `expired_at` column in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and is used to track session lifecycle and validity.

ITodoAppSession.ISummary.description:
Unified summary view of an authenticated session within the todoApp service.

This DTO abstracts over actor-specific session tables, allowing clients and internal tools to render session information without needing to know whether the session belongs to a member user or an admin user. It is designed for list and dashboard contexts where a concise overview of session identity, actor type, connection context, and lifecycle is sufficient.

The schema intentionally includes only stable, non-sensitive fields: a unique session identifier, an actor type discriminator, the owning actor identifier, basic network context, and key timestamps. This makes it suitable for security monitoring, audit logs, and administration UIs while avoiding exposure of implementation details or secrets.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the session record.

For member sessions this corresponds to `todo_app_memberuser_sessions.id`, and for admin sessions it maps to `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.id`. It is used as the canonical key when listing or managing sessions across actor types.

actor_type.description:
High-level classification of the actor who owns this session.

Typical values are `"member"` for regular end users sourced from `todo_app_memberuser_sessions`, and `"admin"` for administrative operators sourced from `todo_app_adminuser_sessions`. This discriminator allows clients to distinguish and filter sessions by actor category.

actor_id.description:
Identifier of the actor who owns this session.

For member sessions this is the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions.todo_app_memberuser_id` value pointing into `todo_app_memberusers`, and for admin sessions it is `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.todo_app_adminuser_id` pointing into `todo_app_adminusers`. It enables correlation between session records and their owning accounts.

ip.description:
IP address recorded when the session was created.

For member sessions the value mirrors `todo_app_memberuser_sessions.ip`, and for administrative sessions it mirrors `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.ip`. It provides the primary network-level indicator used in security monitoring and anomaly detection.

href.description:
Full URL (href) that was accessed when the session was created.

This property reflects either `todo_app_memberuser_sessions.href` or `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.href` depending on actor type. It describes the concrete entry point into the application at authentication time.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client at session creation time.

It corresponds to the `referrer` field in the underlying session table and indicates the previous page or origin that led the actor to the login or protected route.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the session was created.

For member users this value is taken from `todo_app_memberuser_sessions.created_at`, and for admins from `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.created_at`. It marks the start of the authenticated interaction window.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session expired or was explicitly terminated, or null if it is still active.

Aligned with the `expired_at` column of the underlying session table, this field allows consumers to determine session validity and to filter or highlight sessions that are no longer in effect.

ITodoAppTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single todo item in the todoApp service.

This DTO is optimized for list views and lightweight responses. It exposes the most important fields that users need when scanning their todos, such as the title, current state, and key timestamps, without including heavier fields that are only required in full detail views.

The summary is directly backed by the `todo_app_todos` Prisma model and respects its field definitions, nullability, and business rules. It is typically used as the item type in paginated todo lists and as embedded context in other responses that need to reference todos succinctly.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the todo item.

This corresponds to `todo_app_todos.id` and is a UUID primary key generated by the database. Clients use this identifier when performing operations that target a specific todo, such as viewing details, updating, completing, reopening, or deleting the todo.

title.description:
Short human-readable title of the todo.

The title comes from `todo_app_todos.title` and is required non-empty text summarizing the action or task. It is the main field shown in list views and should be concise enough to scan multiple todos quickly.

state.description:
Current business state of the todo item.

This is mapped from `todo_app_todos.state`. Typical conceptual values include states such as "active" or "pending" for open tasks and "completed" for finished tasks. Application logic may also treat rows with `deleted_at` set as logically deleted even if `state` still reflects the last visible state.

Clients primarily use this field to render visual indicators and filter or group todos by status in summary lists.

due_date.description:
Optional target date and time by which the user intends to complete the todo.

This field is backed by `todo_app_todos.due_date` and may be null when the todo has no explicit due date. When present, it is an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or a well-defined timezone. User interfaces typically surface this in list views to highlight upcoming or overdue tasks.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the todo item.

This field reflects `todo_app_todos.created_at` and captures when the todo was first inserted. It is useful for chronological ordering of todos and for displaying metadata such as "created on" in list or detail views.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to this todo.

This value mirrors `todo_app_todos.updated_at` and is updated whenever the todo content or state changes. Client applications can use it to show "last updated" information or to detect that a todo has changed since it was last displayed.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo was most recently completed, if ever.

This field is mapped from `todo_app_todos.completed_at`. It is null when the todo has never been completed or has been reopened without being completed again. When non-null, it records the exact time the todo entered the completed state and can be used for analytics or history views.

ITodoAppAdminUserSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for listing administrative user sessions for the todoApp backend.

This request type is used by the admin session index endpoint to query `todo_app_adminuser_sessions` records belonging to a specific administrative user. It provides pagination controls, optional filtering by creation time, and optional IP address matching to support security monitoring use cases.

The DTO is designed for read-only analytics and dashboards. It never creates or mutates sessions; it only influences how existing session rows are selected and ordered when generating a paginated summary response.

page.description:
Page index for pagination when listing admin user sessions.

Clients generally treat this as a 1-based page number, where `1` represents the first page of results. The server may normalize or clamp invalid values to a sensible default to avoid errors.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return in a single page of results.

This value controls the page size for the query against `todo_app_adminuser_sessions`. Servers should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large result sets that could degrade performance.

fromCreatedAt.description:
Optional inclusive lower bound for the `created_at` timestamp of admin user sessions to include in the result set.

When provided, only sessions whose `created_at` value is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are considered. Use this together with `toCreatedAt` for time-range based investigations.

toCreatedAt.description:
Optional inclusive upper bound for the `created_at` timestamp of admin user sessions to include in the result set.

When provided, only sessions whose `created_at` value is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are considered. Use this together with `fromCreatedAt` for bounded time-window queries.

ip.description:
Optional filter for matching the `ip` column of `todo_app_adminuser_sessions`.

When specified, only sessions whose stored IP address matches this value are returned. This is useful for tracing activity from a specific administrative workstation or network location.

oneOf.description:
Sorting direction for the `created_at` field when ordering admin user sessions in ascending chronological order (oldest first).

Use this value when you want earlier sessions to appear before more recent ones in the result set. This setting affects only the presentation order and does not change any underlying data.

Sorting direction for the `created_at` field when ordering admin user sessions in descending chronological order (newest first).
