ITodoAppGuestUser.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a guest user concept in the todoApp service.

This summary type is used wherever the system needs to reference or display guest user information in a compact form, without exposing full internal auditing details.

Guest users represent unauthenticated or anonymous visitors tracked conceptually by the backend. They never own todos directly and are primarily used in authorization, analytics, or future extension points.

The summary exposes both creation and last update timestamps so that administrative tools and analytics pipelines can reason about the lifecycle and recency of each guest concept record without loading the full entity.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user concept record.

This matches the primary key of the `todo_app_guestusers` table and is used to correlate any optional guest metadata across the system.

external_ref.description:
Optional external reference or correlation identifier for this guest concept.

Typical examples include an anonymous analytics ID or a cookie-based tracking token. When null, no persistent external identifier is associated with this guest record.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this guest concept record was created.

Used for basic auditing, reporting, and retention policies around guest-related data.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating the most recent update to this guest concept record.

This value mirrors the `updated_at` column of the `todo_app_guestusers` table and is useful for understanding when guest-related metadata was last changed and for driving lifecycle or retention heuristics in administrative tooling.

ITodoAppAdminUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an administrative user's authentication session in the todoApp service.

This DTO is optimized for list views and lightweight embeddings where only high-level session information is required rather than full session detail. It exposes the session identifier, the owning admin user context, basic connection metadata, and key lifecycle timestamps so that administrators can quickly scan and audit active or historical sessions.

The summary intentionally omits any heavy or implementation-specific fields and focuses on values that are stable, safe to expose, and useful for monitoring, troubleshooting, and security review flows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin user session.

This value maps directly to `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.id` and is used to reference or revoke a particular administrative session. It is globally unique across all sessions in the todoApp installation.

adminUser.description:
Summary representation of the administrative user who owns this session.

This reference replaces the raw `todo_app_adminuser_id` foreign key and provides immediate context about which admin account established the session, without requiring additional API calls. It allows list views and audit tools to display key admin attributes (such as name or status) alongside each session row.

ip.description:
IP address from which this administrative session was established.

The value comes from `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.ip` and is recorded at the moment the session is created. It is used for security analytics, anomaly detection, and incident investigation workflows.

href.description:
Full request URL that was accessed when the admin session was created.

This directly reflects `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.href` and captures the concrete entry point into the system at login time. It helps operators understand which admin-facing screen initiated authentication.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client when the admin session started.

This maps to `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.referrer` and provides contextual information about how the administrator navigated into the login or protected area, supporting security and UX diagnostics.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the administrative session was created.

It is the direct projection of `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.created_at` and marks the point at which authentication succeeded and the session became valid.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the administrative session expired or was revoked, or null while it remains active.

The value is sourced from `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.expired_at`. A null indicates an active or not-yet-terminated session, whereas a non-null value marks the end of the session's validity window.

ITodoAppMemberUserStatus.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying the business status of a member user account in the todoApp system.

This schema is used exclusively by administrative workflows that need to change the status column of the `todo_app_memberusers` Prisma model while leaving immutable identity fields such as `id` and `email` untouched. Typical status values include `active`, `blocked`, or `disabled`, and they control whether a member is allowed to authenticate and operate on todos.

Implementations should always validate the requested status value against allowed transitions and persist the change in a single transaction that also refreshes the `updated_at` column. This DTO intentionally exposes only the minimal field needed for status management so that administrative clients cannot accidentally modify unrelated profile attributes when calling the status endpoint.

status.description:
New business status value to apply to the member user account.

This string corresponds directly to the `status` column of the `todo_app_memberusers` Prisma model and determines whether the member is considered active, blocked, disabled, or in another well-defined state. Typical implementations constrain this field to a small, predefined set of values such as `active`, `blocked`, and `disabled`.

The backend must validate that the provided status value is recognized and that the transition from the current status to the new status is allowed under configured business rules. Clients should treat this as an opaque but documented enumeration and must not attempt to store user-defined free-form states.
